audit.whatIsWrong: diff was 'HARD' while diffRating said 6/10 and report[14] said 'Even matchup' — and the Emerald+ figure is 51.77% over 1325 games.
audit.why: Three fields gave three different verdicts on the same lane. The win rate and the mixed level chart both read even.
audit.corrected: diff set to EVEN; 6/10 and the report line already agreed with that.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five of the seven level rows were wrong in BOTH layers. The chart said Skill/Skill/Skill/Olaf/Skill/Olaf/Olaf while the packet chart and every one of the matching 'why' strings said Olaf/Skill/Sett/Sett/Olaf/Sett/Skill.
audit.why: whys[2] and whys[3] describe Sett out-chunking and grinding Olaf down, whys[4] describes Olaf's one clean window, whys[5] calls first item 'his most oppressive point' and whys[6] calls two items a coinflip. The sides contradicted the prose sitting next to them.
audit.corrected: All seven rows proposed together as one group, phases[N].side and win[N] in matched pairs, ratings moved to follow, and the four contradicting phase 'why' strings rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named a single Sett ability (the packet flags this as a defect), claimed Ragnarok 'cleanses'/'removes'/'eats' his CC, and called his ultimate an 'R suppress'.
audit.why: Riot's Ragnarok text grants immunity to disables while he keeps attacking — it does not say it cleanses anything already applied. Riot's The Show Stopper text is a carry-and-slam that damages and slows; suppression is not in the text. Most importantly, Facebreaker STUNS only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — a lone laner on one side is merely slowed, which is the decisive interaction the page never stated.
audit.corrected: Named Pit Grit, Knuckle Down, Haymaker, Facebreaker (16s rank 1) and The Show Stopper; stated the both-sides stun rule; replaced every cleanse claim with the immunity-while-attacking wording; dropped 'suppress'; stated that Reckless Swing self-damage refills his Grit bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] headed 'R to cleanse his E stun' had a body about baiting Haymaker.
audit.why: Body did not match its own trigger, and the heading asserted a cleanse.
audit.corrected: Body now states Ragnarok blocks Facebreaker while he keeps swinging.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Sett contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow lets you walk an auto in before Pit Grit's alternating punches ramp — take first contact, then back off.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sett must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Haymaker is stored and Facebreaker is up (16s at rank 1) — his true-damage smash out-chunks your Reckless Swing trades.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Pit Grit's regen plus Haymaker's shield grind your short trades down, and every point of E self-damage refills his Grit bar.

edits.before: Ragnarok deletes CC — once you press R, nothing he has stops the run-down. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sett's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes you immune to disables while you keep swinging, so Facebreaker and The Show Stopper cannot stop the run-down. Your one clean window.

edits.before: Sundered Sky is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Haymaker's cooldown.
edits.after: His bruiser first item plus a full Grit bar out-sustains you — this is his window, not yours.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sett carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in it is a coinflip: your flat true damage stops scaling as his shield grows. Carry threat 7/10 — close it earlier.

edits.before: True-damage him; R cleanses his stun. Track Haymaker before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: True-damage him; R makes you immune to his stun. Track Haymaker before every commit and keep the wave on your side.

edits.before: Sett wastes Haymaker — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Ragnarok blocks Facebreaker while you keep swinging at him.

edits.before: Ragnarok removes his E grab-stun and R suppress, so you all-in through his CC and your passive shreds him.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes you immune to Facebreaker and The Show Stopper while you keep swinging, so you all-in through his CC.

edits.before: Your E true damage stops scaling while his W and R suppress stay relevant, so two-item duels are a coinflip.
edits.after: Your E true damage stops scaling while Haymaker's shield grows off your damage, so two-item duels are a coinflip.

edits.before: Ragnarok (R) eats his E grab-stun and his R suppress, turning his all-in into your free dive — your hardest window.
edits.after: Ragnarok makes you immune to Facebreaker and The Show Stopper while you keep swinging — his all-in becomes your free dive.

edits.before: Open with Undertow (Q) — the slow lets you walk an auto onto Sett before his passive rhythm gets going, and you can pick the axe back up to keep him slowed. Don't sit in extended trades at level 1-2: Sett's passive double-punch and his grit shield ramp the longer you swing, and your E self-damage feeds his W charge. Poke with Q-auto-disengage, keep the axe between you, and refuse to fight where he can E-grab you into a wall.
edits.after: Open with Undertow (Q) — the slow lets you walk an auto onto Sett before Pit Grit's rhythm gets going, and picking the axe back up resets it. Don't sit in extended trades at level 1-2: his alternating punches and Grit shield ramp the longer you swing, and every point of Reckless Swing self-damage is Grit he cashes back. Facebreaker only stuns when enemies are on both sides of him — stand clear of the minion line and it is only a slow.

edits.before: This is Sett's window, not yours — by levels 3-5 he has W stored, his passive is punching every other auto, and his true-damage smash out-chunks your E-Reckless-Swing trades since E costs you health he heals off your damage. Respect his E grab-stun; if he lands it you eat the full empowered punch and W combo. Hold your ground only when his W is empty and his E is down. Then at 6 the lane flips for one moment: Ragnarok cancels his E-stun and his R suppress, so save it, bait his all-in, and ult through it to run him down with your passive attack speed ramping.
edits.after: This is Sett's window, not yours — by levels 3-5 he has Haymaker stored, Pit Grit is punching every other auto, and his true-damage smash out-chunks your Reckless Swing trades since E costs you health he cashes as Grit. Respect Facebreaker (16s at rank 1); if he catches you between himself and a minion it stuns instead of slowing and the full Haymaker follows. Hold your ground only when his Grit bar is empty and Facebreaker is down. At 6 the lane flips for one moment: Ragnarok makes you immune to disables while you keep swinging, so bait his all-in and ult through it with your passive attack speed ramping.

edits.before: Past first item Sett's stored W plus his bruiser sustain out-grinds your short-trade kit, and your flat E true damage stops scaling while he keeps a teamfight-relevant R suppress. You don't out-scale him, so your job is to cash your level 6 R window into kills, plates, or a herald before two items — once he's full bruiser the straight 1v1 is a coinflip you'd rather not take. In skirmishes, Ragnarok still lets you ignore his R to dive past him onto a backliner.
edits.after: Past first item Sett's stored Haymaker plus his bruiser sustain out-grinds your short-trade kit, and your flat E true damage stops scaling while The Show Stopper stays teamfight-relevant. You don't out-scale him, so your job is to cash your level 6 R window into kills, plates, or a herald before two items — once he's full bruiser the straight 1v1 is a coinflip you'd rather not take. In skirmishes, Ragnarok still lets you keep swinging through his ultimate onto a backliner.

edits.after: Save Ragnarok for Facebreaker into Haymaker and keep swinging through it

edits.after: Catch you between him and a minion so Facebreaker stuns instead of only slowing

notes: Both level-chart layers agreed with each other but disagreed with the packet chart AND with their own adjacent prose on five of seven rows; all seven rows are proposed as one paired group. Whether The Show Stopper suppresses (rather than merely displaces) is not in Riot's text, so no text asserts it. Whether Undertow's grounding stops The Show Stopper's leap is also unverified and is left unstated.
